Based on your setup — **Sony A7R IV**, **Sony 24-70mm f/2.8**, **Godox V1**, and the **Gitzo GT3543LS** tripod you were considering — here's what would round it out:

**Support & stability**
- **Ball head + quick-release plate** — the GT3543LS is a Systematic *leg set* with no head included, so budget for a solid ball head (RRS BH-40/55 or Gitzo GH3382QD) if you go that route.
- **Arca-Swiss L-bracket** (RRS, Kirk, SmallRig) — lets you flip to portrait on the tripod without recomposing; pays off with the A7R IV's 61MP files.
- **Wired remote / intervalometer** — cleaner than the phone app for long exposures and pixel-shift work.

**Flash system (Godox V1)**
- **Godox XPro-S or X2T-S trigger** for off-camera flash.
- **Spare WB26 battery** + a compact stand/umbrella or S2 bracket + softbox.
- **AK-R1 round-head accessory kit** (gels, grids, diffusion) — cheap and very useful with the round head.

**Glass protection & effects**
- **82mm circular polarizer and a 3- or 6-stop ND** for the 24-70 (or a magnetic system with step-up rings).
- **Rocket blower + sensor swabs** to go with your existing microfiber cleaning routine (the A7R IV shows dust easily).

**Power & storage**
- **Spare NP-FZ100 batteries + dual USB-C charger** (pairs with the PD battery pack you looked into).
- **UHS-II V90 SD cards** — both slots are UHS-II and 61MP RAWs are big.
- A **USB-C PD wall charger** so one charger covers camera batteries, phone, and power bank.

**Carrying & field use**
- **Camera bag** — this is still the open item. If you tell me budget, how much gear you carry (body + 24-70 + V1 + tripod), and backpack vs. messenger, I can shortlist options.
- **Peak Design Capture clip or Slide/Leash strap** for hiking/kayaking days — quick access and keeps the camera off your neck.
- **Rain cover or dry bag** — worth having given the weather sealing gap on the V1 and your Teton paddling trip.

Want me to focus on the camera bag shortlist or the tripod head pairing first?
